decisions.rationale: Metaethical family should remain a derived synthesis over independently measured metaethical commitments; MEI005 is diagnostic, not a standalone family scale.

construct.name: Metaethical family
construct.description: Derived classification over realist, constructivist, subjectivist, error-theoretic, noncognitivist, and related families.

decisions.rationale: Liberty/opposition-to-domination is theoretically interesting, but it is not part of the standard MFQ-2 six-foundation model and the current items are original exploratory content.

construct.name: Liberty / opposition to domination
construct.description: Experimental moral-foundation construct concerning domination, coercion, and liberty.

decisions.rationale: Existing items directly ask whether knowledge is simple versus interconnected/developing; interpret only this narrow personal-epistemology proposition.

construct.name: Knowledge complexity
construct.description: Tendency to regard knowledge as complex, interconnected, and developing rather than simple and fixed.

decisions.rationale: EPI015 was already excluded and the remaining material does not provide two independent negative indicators of truth attainability without conflating approximation, skepticism, and conventionalism.

construct.name: Attainability of truth
construct.description: Confidence that objective truth or knowledge is attainable in principle.

decisions.rationale: Two direct, opposing items support a narrow a-priori-justification interpretation; EPI025 remains excluded as a knowledge/trivia recognition question.

construct.name: Rational / a priori reliance
construct.description: Epistemic weight assigned to reason, conceptual analysis, or a priori justification.

decisions.rationale: Public systematic testability can be interpreted as an epistemic preference, without claiming science is the only source of knowledge.

construct.name: Scientific-method reliance
construct.description: Epistemic weight assigned to systematic scientific methods.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly ask whether purported revelation can provide factual justification; this is distinct from revelation's moral or political authority.

construct.name: Revelation as epistemic source
construct.description: Epistemic weight assigned to alleged divine or supernatural revelation.

decisions.rationale: The current construct conflates external-world metaphysics, perceptual directness, and skepticism. Retain narrower external-world-independence and skepticism interpretations; do not emit one categorical label.

construct.name: External-world stance
construct.description: Direct realism, indirect realism, idealism, skepticism, or related positions regarding the external world.

decisions.rationale: Substantive-versus-deflationary attitudes can be reported, but framework relativity and verbalism should not be collapsed into one categorical metaontology label.

construct.name: Metaontology
construct.description: Whether ontological disputes are substantive, deflationary, quantifier-relative, or otherwise construed.

decisions.rationale: Identity-under-transformation is appropriately a derived pattern over continuity and transformation cases; one teleportation item cannot support a direct scale.

construct.name: Identity under transformation
construct.description: Derived pattern across teleportation, copying, uploading, replacement, and continuity vignettes.

decisions.rationale: Current free-will items partly encode compatibilist conditions, so disagreement may mean incompatibilism rather than disbelief in free will.

construct.name: Free-will belief
construct.description: Strength of belief that human agents possess free will.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address basic/desert-entailing responsibility and manipulation; keep distinct from forward-looking responsibility.

construct.name: Moral-responsibility belief
construct.description: Strength of belief in basic or desert-entailing moral responsibility.

decisions.rationale: The broad 'baseline benevolence' label overreaches. Existing direct items can support only the narrower claim that humans are capable of genuinely other-regarding motivation.

construct.name: Baseline human benevolence
construct.description: Belief that humans are naturally capable of or inclined toward benevolence/cooperation.

decisions.rationale: Self-interest prevalence and competition are different. Psychological egoism is already represented by AH13 and social competition by SO08; do not score this bundled construct as one worldview dimension.

construct.name: Baseline human selfishness / competition
construct.description: Belief that humans are naturally inclined toward selfishness, rivalry, or competition.

decisions.rationale: Existing items directly concern malleability of human dispositions; keep separate from whether causes are biological or environmental.

construct.name: Human-nature mutability
construct.description: Belief that human traits and dispositions are substantially malleable.

decisions.rationale: A generic preference for multi-causal explanation is a methodological outlook with no clear validated worldview construct here; retain for research only.

construct.name: Human-nature complexity
construct.description: Belief that behavior resists simple, single-cause accounts.

decisions.rationale: Interpret only the reported belief that biological/inherited factors can make substantial causal contributions; do not infer immutability or normativity.

construct.name: Biological causal attribution
construct.description: Weight assigned to biological and inherited causes of behavior.

decisions.rationale: Interpret only the reported belief that social/environmental factors can substantially shape behavior; do not infer blank-slate views.

construct.name: Environmental / social causal attribution
construct.description: Weight assigned to environmental, institutional, and social causes of behavior.

decisions.rationale: Compatibilist/libertarian/skeptical family classification must remain derived from free-will, determinism, and responsibility answers.

construct.name: Agency theory family
construct.description: Derived but explicitly confirmed classification among compatibilist, libertarian, hard-determinist, skeptical, and related positions.

decisions.rationale: Conditional questions directly distinguish personal/agentic from impersonal divinity; only interpret when relevant branch prerequisites are satisfied.

construct.name: Personal / agentic deity
construct.description: Degree to which divinity is understood as personal, intentional, or agentic.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address whether supernatural agency can intervene in ordinary events.

construct.name: Divine / supernatural intervention
construct.description: Belief that supernatural agency intervenes in ordinary events.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address miracles, while distinguishing unexplained natural events from miracle claims.

construct.name: Miraculous intervention
construct.description: Belief that events can occur through suspension or extraordinary override of ordinary natural regularities.

decisions.rationale: Current items support a narrow claim about purported revelation having authority for belief or conduct, distinct from public-law authority.

construct.name: Revelatory authority
construct.description: Authority granted to purported revelation in belief and conduct.

decisions.rationale: Theism, deism, pantheism, panentheism, and impersonal divinity are a family of alternatives. Keep the family descriptive/derived rather than a single score.

construct.name: Divinity model
construct.description: Theistic, deistic, pantheistic, panentheistic, impersonal-divinity, and related models.

decisions.rationale: Designer-grounded and non-designer sources of objective purpose should be separate commitments, not one categorical score.

construct.name: Objective-purpose source
construct.description: Proposed source of objective meaning or purpose when such meaning is endorsed.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly distinguish denial of objective/inherent meaning from alternative objective or constructed sources.

construct.name: Existential nihilism
construct.description: Degree of endorsement that life lacks objective or inherent meaning/value.

decisions.rationale: World-safety is a validated Primal World Beliefs construct, but these are custom items and should remain explicitly exploratory until calibrated.

construct.name: World safety
construct.description: General belief that the world is safe rather than dangerous.

decisions.rationale: World-aliveness is a validated primal family, but these custom items mix felt intentionality and metaphysical responsiveness; retain as research-only.

construct.name: World aliveness / intentional character
construct.description: General tendency to experience the world as intentional, responsive, or alive.

decisions.rationale: The current scale mixes social improvability, personal problems, and pessimism; it is not a clean optimism measure.

construct.name: Optimism vs resignation
construct.description: General orientation toward possibility of improvement versus resignation or pessimism.

decisions.rationale: Responses to meaninglessness should be derived from meaning/nihilism responses rather than scored as an independent latent trait.

construct.name: Response to meaninglessness
construct.description: Derived existential style in response to absence or uncertainty of objective meaning.

decisions.rationale: Existing items directly ask whether relationships/roles partly constitute identity; do not equate this with collectivism.

construct.name: Relational / interdependent self
construct.description: Degree to which identity is understood through constitutive relationships and social roles.

decisions.rationale: Interpret narrowly as toleration/noninterference toward disliked non-rights-violating ways of life, not generalized warmth toward outgroups.

construct.name: Tolerance of otherness
construct.description: Acceptance of persons, lifestyles, and groups substantially different from one's own.

decisions.rationale: Current items align conceptually with group-dominance preference; custom wording is not an SDO-7 administration.

construct.name: Group-dominance preference
construct.description: Preference for hierarchical dominance of some social groups over others.

decisions.rationale: Current items align with opposition to group equality as a distinct SDO-related tendency; do not infer explicit dominance.

construct.name: Anti-egalitarianism
construct.description: Opposition to group-based social equality independent of explicit dominance preference.

decisions.rationale: General cooperation preference is not equivalent to validated Social Value Orientation allocation behavior; retain for research.

construct.name: Cooperation orientation
construct.description: Belief in and preference for cooperative modes of social interaction.

decisions.rationale: General competition preference is not equivalent to SVO or a single economic ideology; retain for research.

construct.name: Competition orientation
construct.description: Belief in and preference for competitive modes of social interaction.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address moral scope across group boundaries; distinguish from institutional cosmopolitanism and absence of special obligations.

construct.name: Scope of moral concern / cosmopolitan concern
construct.description: Breadth of the circle of persons toward whom substantial moral concern is extended.

decisions.rationale: Current items support a narrow psychological-essentialism interpretation; do not infer biological determinism or stereotype endorsement.

construct.name: Social-category essentialism
construct.description: Degree to which social categories are treated as deep, natural, fixed, or essence-bearing.

decisions.rationale: Humanity-nature worldview is hierarchical. Existing items support ecological interdependence and anthropocentric-priority subclaims, not one total ecological score.

construct.name: Humanity-nature worldview
construct.description: Higher-order family containing anthropocentrism, ecocentrism, ecological limits, mastery, and harmony/interdependence facets.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address general just-world belief; do not infer personal just-world belief or victim blaming.

construct.name: Belief in social/world justice
construct.description: Belief that people generally receive outcomes they deserve or that social reality is fundamentally just.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly ask whether political institutions can possess a moral right to coerce; keep distinct from political obligation.

construct.name: Legitimacy of coercive political authority
construct.description: Degree to which states or political institutions can possess a justified right to coerce.

decisions.rationale: Interpret as centralization/decentralization preference in stated governance contexts, not as a complete theory of federalism.

construct.name: Centralization vs decentralization
construct.description: Preference for concentration versus dispersion of political decision-making authority.

decisions.rationale: Equality, need, desert, sufficiency, priority, and entitlement are different distributive principles. Ranking them does not justify one family score.

construct.name: Distributive-principle family
construct.description: Relative affinities for equality, need, desert, sufficiency, priority, entitlement, and related distributive principles.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address legitimacy of common ownership; do not infer socialism or rejection of private property in all domains.

construct.name: Collective / common ownership legitimacy
construct.description: Degree to which common, collective, or social ownership is regarded as legitimate or desirable.

decisions.rationale: Interpret as preference for participatory/democratic coordination in stated contexts, not as endorsement of political democracy everywhere.

construct.name: Collective / democratic coordination preference
construct.description: Preference for collective, participatory, or democratically planned coordination.

decisions.rationale: Interpret as preference for expert/administrative decision authority in stated contexts, distinct from valuing expert testimony.

construct.name: Expert / administrative coordination preference
construct.description: Preference for expert, technocratic, or administrative coordination.

decisions.rationale: Current items directly address deterrence as a purpose/justification of punishment; mixed theories remain possible.

construct.name: Deterrent punishment
construct.description: Support for punishment as a means of deterring future wrongdoing.

decisions.rationale: Rehabilitation and restorative repair are distinct aims. Current direct items bundle them, so do not emit one combined score.

construct.name: Rehabilitative / restorative punishment
construct.description: Support for rehabilitation, repair, restoration, or reintegration as purposes of criminal justice.

decisions.rationale: Interpret as gradual reform versus decisive institutional replacement; do not equate rupture with violent revolution.

construct.name: Reform vs rupture orientation
construct.description: Preference for gradual institutional reform versus discontinuous or revolutionary replacement.

questionProposals.reason: Need a second independent negative indicator that distinguishes skepticism about knowability from approximation and domain-limited uncertainty.
items: There are at least some factual questions for which sufficiently good inquiry can yield knowledge that the answer is objectively correct.
Human inquiry may approach better explanations, but it can never know any factual answer to be objectively correct.

questionProposals.reason: Need direct free-will existence items that do not presuppose compatibilism or incompatibilism.
items: Human beings possess at least some genuine control over action that deserves to be called free will, whatever the correct theory of that control is.
Human behavior never involves the kind of control that would count as genuine free will.

questionProposals.reason: The existing construct bundles self-interest and competition; AH13 already measures psychological egoism and SO08 covers competition.
items: Even when cooperation is available, people usually pursue their own advantage as a default motive.
Competition is a common default pattern of interaction even when nobody is forced into it.

questionProposals.reason: The six distributive principles need direct, non-ranking indicators so a single top-choice task does not define an affinity.
items: When no stronger claim applies, making people's shares more equal is itself a reason in favor of a distribution.
Greater need is itself a reason to give someone a larger share.
Greater contribution or desert is itself a reason to give someone a larger share.
Ensuring that everyone has enough can matter more than reducing inequality above that threshold.
Benefits to people who are worse off can deserve extra weight even when total gains are smaller.
A person's legitimate prior entitlement can justify an unequal share even when another distribution would be more equal.

questionProposals.reason: Rehabilitation and restorative repair are distinct purposes and need separate direct indicators.
items: Changing an offender's capacities and dispositions so future wrongdoing is less likely is itself an important aim of a just response.
Repairing harm among victims, offenders, and affected communities is itself an important aim of justice after wrongdoing.
